articleBody:
- [ ] Ensure everyone's safety — why: Your immediate priority is the well-being of yourself and others; move to a safe spot if possible.
- [ ] Call 911 (or local emergency number) — why: Report the accident, especially if there are injuries or significant damage, and get an official police report.
- [ ] Exchange information — why: Collect names, contact details, insurance information, and license plate numbers from all involved parties.
- [ ] Document the scene thoroughly — why: Take photos of vehicle damage, road conditions, traffic signals, and any visible injuries; these are crucial for evidence.
- [ ] Seek medical attention immediately — why: Even if you feel fine, some injuries have delayed symptoms, and a medical record connects your injuries to the accident.
- [ ] Notify your insurance company — why: Inform your own insurer about the accident, but be cautious about giving detailed statements without legal advice.
- [ ] Keep a detailed record of expenses — why: Track all medical bills, lost wages, and other accident-related costs to ensure full compensation.
- [ ] Avoid discussing fault — why: Never admit fault or make assumptions; stick to facts when speaking with others or insurance adjusters.
- [ ] Consult a San Diego Car Accident Lawyer — why: An experienced attorney can protect your rights, deal with insurance companies, and help you understand the true value of your claim.

How to use this checklist: This checklist is designed to help you navigate the confusing and stressful moments right after a car accident. Go through each item methodically to ensure you've covered all your bases. Checking off each point can help you stay organized, protect your health, and safeguard your potential legal claim. Remember, this is a guide, and seeking professional legal advice is always recommended for personal injury cases.
